Run your own server#

Verse ships as one container: the playground, the embed SDK, the docs site, the ingest API with the native compiler, Ed25519 signing, share links, review comments, presence rooms, telemetry. Point the exporters and the embed script at your origin and nothing else changes — the protocol is identical to the hosted service.

You need: Docker, a host that can terminate HTTPS, and a persistent disk for the ingest volume. Node 22 and Rust are only needed for the no-Docker path.

Hard requirements#

RequirementWhyIf missing
HTTPS (or localhost)WebGPU, service workers and SharedArrayBuffer need a secure contextnothing renders
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin + Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp on every engine documentSharedArrayBuffer for the sim↔render triple bufferengine falls back to a single worker (slower, still works)
HTTP Range requests reach the origin untouchedstreaming is byte-range fetches of the .vpkthe runtime refuses the host ("range not honored")
Exactly one replicarate limits, the job map and the compile semaphore are in memoryduplicated state, lost jobs

serve.mjs sets the headers itself; a reverse proxy must pass them (and Range) through.

1. Build and run with Docker#

Code
docker build -t verse-engine .
docker run -d --name verse -p 8080:8080 \
  -v verse-ingest:/app/web/playground/ingest \
  verse-engine
curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/health/deep
# → {"ok":true,"checks":{"volumeWritable":true,"compilerPresent":true,"signingKey":true, …}}

The multi-stage Dockerfile builds both wasm tiers (WebGPU and the WebGL2 fallback), the native verse-compile and splat-pack binaries, precompresses the engine, and pins + sha256-verifies the vendored Draco and Basis codecs. Build time is 5–7 minutes; the Rust stage dominates.

The volume at /app/web/playground/ingest is the product: compiled .vpk/.vsp scenes, posters, tours, experiences, review comments, and the operational dotfiles (signing key, API keys, usage, telemetry log). It must persist across deploys. The entrypoint fixes the mount's ownership and drops to the unprivileged node user.

Compiled scenes can live in an S3-compatible bucket instead of the volume (this is how the hosted service runs): set VERSE_STORAGE=s3 and the VERSE_S3_* variables below. Metadata (keys, accounts, usage, reviews, telemetry) and compiler scratch stay on the volume, so it is still required. Scene bytes are proxied through the origin by default (range requests, signing and private-scene rules unchanged); VERSE_S3_REDIRECT=1 restores the older 302 to the object URL. Provisioning, migration, backups and rollback: docs/storage.md in the repository.

Without Docker (development)#

Code
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
wasm-pack build crates/verse-web --target web --profile wasm-release --out-dir ../../web/playground/pkg
wasm-pack build crates/verse-web --target web --profile wasm-release --out-dir ../../web/playground/pkg-gl -- --no-default-features --features webgl
scripts/build-codecs.sh   # JPEG / WebP / HDR codec module (loaded on first need), next to both tiers
cargo build --release -p verse-compile --bins
node web/playground/serve.mjs                   # http://localhost:8080

Vendored codecs (web/playground/vendor/) and the sample helmet are fetched by the commands in DEPLOY.md §3–4.

2. Environment variables#

All optional. The server runs with sensible defaults and no configuration.

Server#

VariableDefaultEffect
PORT8080listen port
VERSE_SIGNING_KEYauto-generated on the volumebase64 PKCS8 DER Ed25519 key that signs every compiled scene. Set it from a secret store in production; a malformed value refuses to start. Generate: node -e 'console.log(require("node:crypto").generateKeyPairSync("ed25519").privateKey.export({type:"pkcs8",format:"der"}).toString("base64"))'
VERSE_INGEST_PER_HOUR6anonymous uploads per hour per IP (loopback exempt)
VERSE_INGEST_PER_HOUR_TOKEN20uploads per hour per account token — independent of IP
VERSE_UPLOAD_STALE_MS2 hidle time before a resumable upload expires
VERSE_VPK_BUDGET_MB3500disk budget for compiled scenes; over it, the least-recently-opened unowned scene is evicted. Owned scenes are never evicted
VERSE_MIN_FREE_MB1024free-space floor; uploads are refused with 507 when free space is below max(this, 3× upload size)
VERSE_SWEEP_MS15 minsweeper cadence (compile intermediates, stale uploads, finished job records, canary artifacts)
VERSE_MAX_POSTERS / VERSE_MAX_TOURS / VERSE_MAX_EXPERIENCES500 / 1000 / 1000newest-N caps on published sidecars
VERSE_CDN_BASEunsethttps origin of an edge cache; public .vpk/.vsp GETs 302 there, /v1/config hands it to the client. See CDN
VERSE_STORAGEvolumes3 stores compiled scenes in an S3-compatible bucket (see above)
VERSE_S3_BUCKET / VERSE_S3_ENDPOINT / VERSE_S3_REGION / VERSE_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID / VERSE_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEYunsetthe bucket and its credentials (VERSE_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE, VERSE_S3_PREFIX optional)
VERSE_S3_REDIRECTunset1 answers public scene GETs with a 302 to the bucket instead of proxying the bytes (the pre-2026-10-12 behaviour)
VERSE_CDN_RANGESunset0 keeps ranged requests on the origin for a CDN that cannot serve 206
VERSE_TELEMETRY_URL (+ VERSE_TELEMETRY_AUTH)unsetbatch-forward telemetry as ndjson every 15 s (ClickHouse-HTTP compatible); the local JSONL keeps being written
VERSE_WORKER_TOKENunsetenables /v1/work/* so external tools/verse-worker boxes pull compile jobs. Unset = compiles run in-process
VERSE_CLASSIC_FALLBACK_MB96largest prepared model the lossless fallback publishes in compatibility mode when every build attempt fails; 0 disables the fallback (jobs then fail with a friendly error)
VERSE_COMPILE_STALL_S600stall watchdog: a compile with no output and no CPU time for this many seconds is killed and retried
VERSE_SLACK_WEBHOOKunset (falls back to VERSE_ALERT_WEBHOOK)Slack incoming-webhook URL: upload received, contact attached, live, healing, failure. See Monitor production
VERSE_RESEND_API_KEY + VERSE_MAIL_FROMunsetResend API key and sender (e.g. Verse Engine <hello@ctruh.com>) for the "email me when it's live" notice. Unset = nothing is sent and nothing fails
VERSE_MAIL_REPLY_TOunsetoptional Reply-To for those emails
VERSE_OPS_ACCOUNTSunsetcomma-separated account ids allowed to read GET /v1/ops/leads (the admin token always may)
SIM_LATENCY_MS0dev only: delay every Range response to reproduce real-internet RTT

Compiler (texture streaming)#

verse-compile reads these from the server's environment. The defaults suit a 2-core box with the 30-minute compile attempt (45-minute job wall clock); raise them on a bigger machine or an external worker.

VariableDefaultEffect
VERSE_STREAM_TEXTURES256how many materials (the most important by world surface area) get full streamed textures; the rest live on the 1024² preview atlas
VERSE_STREAM_BUDGET_MB768byte budget for the encoded streamed texture blobs; selection stops at whichever limit — count or bytes — hits first
VERSE_STREAM_DEADLINE_SECS600wall-clock budget for the texture phase before the compiler degrades to the fast path
VERSE_ENCODE_THREADS2 (clamped 1–8)parallel texture encoders; each costs RAM
VERSE_HERO_TEXTURES / VERSE_HERO_DIM12 / 4096the top-N materials whose source is at least HERO_DIM are kept at 4096² for the tier-A hero pool instead of 2048²
VERSE_TEX_SAFEunsetset by the server itself on the last rung of the self-healing ladder: low-memory ETC1S texture path
VERSE_ENCODE_CACHE_DIRingest/.encode-cache (set by the server)encoded-texture cache: each streamed blob is stored keyed by a SHA-256 of its source bytes, factors, size and encoder settings, so re-uploading a scene skips the texture encode — the longest phase of a compile. Checksummed on read; output is byte-identical to a cold compile. Set to empty to disable. The finished job record reports stats.texCache: {hits, misses}
VERSE_ENCODE_CACHE_MB4096cache size bound; least-recently-used entries (by mtime, bumped on every hit) are evicted after each compile

Access control#

Create ingest/.verse-keys.json on the volume to switch ingest from open mode to keyed mode (X-API-Key required, per-key daily quota):

Code
{ "vk_example123": { "name": "acme-storefront", "quotaMB": 1024 } }

Accounts (POST /v1/account) work in either mode and add ownership, /studio, private scenes and share tokens on top — see the API reference.

3. Verify#

Code
BASE=https://your.origin
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null "$BASE/" | grep -i "cross-origin"        # COOP + COEP present
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/health/deep"                                       # {"ok":true,…}
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/pubkey"                                            # {"alg":"Ed25519","spki":"MCow…"} — must be stable across restarts
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/ingest" -H "Content-Type: model/gltf-binary" \
  -H "X-Verse-Name: smoke" --data-binary @web/playground/test-blend.glb   # → 202 {"job":"smoke-…"}

A spki that changes after a redeploy means the signing key was not persisted (no env var and the dotfile not on a volume) and every earlier scene will report signed: false.

Then open https://your.origin/ — the landing page — and /app, drop a GLB, and confirm the status line ends in " · signed".

4. Put a CDN in front#

Streaming is RTT-bound. An edge cache near the viewer roughly halves time-to-sharp for remote viewers. The server is already CDN-correct — public, max-age=31536000, immutable + strong ETags + Accept-Ranges on public /ingest/*, no-store on /v1/* and on every byte of a private scene — so the operator's half is DNS, cache rules and (optionally) VERSE_CDN_BASE. Put any CDN that honours Cache-Control and byte ranges in front of the origin.

5. Deploying on Railway#

The repo's railway.json and Dockerfile are configured for it: railway up --detach, a volume mounted at /app/web/playground/ingest, overlapSeconds: 0 (the volume forces stop-then-start; expect ~20 s of 502 per deploy), one replica. The hosted service adds a Railway bucket with VERSE_STORAGE=s3 for compiled scenes; the volume keeps the metadata.
